sections.h2: Which Henderson County, KY office does what with a tax bill?
sections.html:
Three county offices take turns with the same bill. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) fixes what a parcel is worth, the Sheriff's Office sends the bill and takes payment, and the County Clerk's Office keeps whatever is left unpaid.

The county attorney's tax collection FAQ gives the timeline. Real estate notices are mailed in late October or early November, and the sheriff accepts payment from November 1. A bill turns delinquent on January 1 after its due date. The sheriff holds the file until uncollected bills are turned over to the clerk, and from that point the clerk's office maintains them.

The county's own wording ties delinquency to two conditions: the due date has passed and any appeal rights have expired. A seller with an unresolved value dispute should therefore treat the appeal calendar and the payment calendar as running side by side.

sections.h2: What sets Henderson County apart from other Kentucky counties?
sections.html:
Henderson County sits in far western Kentucky on the Ohio River, facing Evansville, Indiana, and it is part of the Evansville, IN-KY metropolitan area. Its seat and largest city is Henderson, which grew from a riverside settlement called Red Banks. The county was carved out of Christian County in December 1798 and named for Richard Henderson of the Transylvania Company.

It measures 466 square miles, about 30 of which are water, and lies in the West Kentucky Coal Field. Corydon and Robards are the other incorporated cities, and Anthoston, Poole and Spottsville are census-designated places. Roughly 45 square miles called Green River Island lie on the Indiana bank yet belong to Henderson County, and Ellis Park Race Course occupies part of that ground.

Tobacco built the early town. Around 1880 Henderson counted 17 stemmeries and was the largest dark tobacco market in the world, and production fell through the twentieth century. The 2020 count of 44,793 residents was 3.2 percent below 2010.

Population density is 102.7 people per square mile, and 63.5 percent of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census. Hart County, by comparison, was 11.7 percent urban, so a Henderson seller is marketing in a far more urban county.

sections.h2: What local resources matter when you sell in Henderson County?
sections.html:
The county's links page lists the agencies a seller or buyer is likely to contact.

  • The Henderson City-County Planning Commission oversees public and private development inside both city and county limits.
  • Henderson GIS offers maps, data and information on the county.
  • Henderson County Schools and Henderson Community College anchor education.
  • The Henderson County Riverport and the Henderson City-County Airport, a general aviation field, serve industry and business users.
  • Audubon State Park, the Tourist Commission and the Downtown Henderson Partnership, begun in 1986 with Main Street program support, cover recreation and downtown life.
  • The Henderson Area Board of Realtors and the Housing Authority of Henderson are listed among community organizations.

If a buyer asks about zoning or development near your parcel, point them to the planning commission, and send questions about the tax bill itself to the sheriff or PVA.

sections.h2: How do Henderson County housing figures read?
sections.html:
The typical Henderson County home is valued above Hart County's $146,000 and below Henry County's $197,900. About 37 percent of occupied homes were rented at the 2020 census, which is a meaningful rental market next to the owner-occupied majority.

The county employed 16,375 people at 966 employer establishments in 2023. Retail sales in 2022 were about $763 million and health care and social assistance receipts about $312 million. Of adults 25 and over, 89.7 percent finished high school and 20.1 percent have a bachelor's degree. The poverty rate is 15.7 percent, and 7.2 percent of residents under 65 lack health insurance.

sections.h2: What happens after a Henderson County bill goes delinquent?
sections.html:
Interest and penalties begin, a lien attaches, and an outside buyer may purchase the debt. The county attorney's tax collection FAQ describes each stage.

  • The bill moves to the County Clerk's Office at 20 N Main Street, 2nd Floor, Henderson, where interest of 1 percent per month and penalties accumulate.
  • A lien stays on the property until payment in full.
  • Any individual or company qualified under KRS Chapter 134 may buy the bill at the clerk's tax sale. The clerk cannot predict or prevent that purchase.
  • The purchaser has 50 days to notify the owner. The owner then pays the purchaser, who sends a release to the clerk for recording.
  • A foreclosure suit by the purchaser becomes possible one year after the certificate of delinquency was created.

You can pay the clerk in person or mail a personal check, cashier's check, money order or certified check. Cards work for an added fee, and the clerk's number for details is 270-827-5753. American Express, Discover and MasterCard are taken, and Visa only as a debit.

sections.h2: Who can contest a Henderson County assessment, and how?
sections.html:
The owner starts with a conference at the PVA's office, a step KRS 133.120 places ahead of any formal appeal. The conference happens during or before the inspection window, and the Department of Revenue may allow up to 25 extra days.

If that fails, a written petition goes to the county clerk, and the appeals board holds a public hearing and fixes fair cash value. The county attorney speaks for the state and county there. Someone who loses may go on to the Board of Tax Appeals, but only after appearing before the county board.

Paid representatives must fall into listed categories such as attorney, accountant, tax consultant, owner's employee, broker or certified appraiser. They carry written authorization and disclose any contingency fee, although attorneys need not state its terms. The board can also raise a value, but it must first send the owner notice and a hearing date.

sections.h2: How should a seller handle taxes at a Henderson County closing?
sections.html:
Ownership on January 1 decides whose name goes on the year's bill, and under KRS 134.015 the debt is personal to that owner while a delinquency lien under KRS 134.420 outlasts any sale. Line up both numbers before the closing date: what the sheriff shows for the current year and what the clerk shows for earlier ones.

If a prior year sits with the clerk, the 1 percent monthly interest becomes part of the payoff, so ask for a fresh figure close to the signing. The title agent can pay the total out of your proceeds. For recording charges and the real estate transfer tax on the deed, see the Henderson County Clerk page, which lists the current fee schedule.

faqs.q: When does Henderson County start taking property tax payments?
faqs.a: November 1. Notices go out in late October or early November, and the sheriff accepts payment beginning that day. A bill goes delinquent on the following January 1.

faqs.q: Where is a delinquent Henderson County bill paid?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's Office, 20 N Main Street, 2nd Floor Offices, Henderson, KY 42420. Mailed payments must be a check, money order or other certified funds.

faqs.q: How much interest does the clerk charge on a delinquent bill?
faqs.a: One percent per month plus penalties. A buyer of the bill at the tax sale may add charges allowed under Kentucky law.

faqs.q: Can someone else buy my delinquent Henderson County tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Any person or company qualified under KRS Chapter 134 can buy it at the clerk's sale, and the clerk can neither predict nor stop the purchase.

faqs.q: How long before a bill buyer can foreclose?
faqs.a: One year after the certificate of delinquency is created. Some buyers wait longer while the property's equity covers the debt.
